COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
D￾24 WPMS No. 1495 of 2025
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Shekhar Nanavaty, Advocate for 
the petitioners.
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for the 
respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, Deputy 
Advocate General for the State.
Heard.
Admit.
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate takes 
notice for the respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Learned CSC takes notice for the 
respondent no. 3.
Counter affidavit to be filed within 
four weeks.
Two weeks thereafter, rejoinder 
affidavit, if any, may be filed.
List thereafter.
Heard on stay application (IA No. 1 of 
2025).
The challenge in this petition is made 
to the order dated 22.04.2025 passed by 
the appellate authority under Section 340 
of the Cantonments Act, 2006 as well as 
the notice issued by the Cantonment 
Board, Dehradun under Section 248 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006.
Proceedings under the Cantonments 
Act, 2006 were initiated for demolition of 
certain property. Demolition order was 
passed, which was unsuccessfully assailed  in the appeal. The property has already 
been sealed since 2019. 
Learned counsel for the petitioner 
would submit that the petitioner has all the 
chances to success in the matter, therefore, 
till the matter is finally heard, the operation 
of the impugned order may be kept in 
abeyance.
Learned counsel for the Cantonment 
Board would submit that status quo order 
may be passed and the property may 
remain sealed as such.
Having considered, till the next date 
of listing, as an interim order, it is directed 
that no demolition shall be done and the 
status quo shall be maintained with regard 
to the property in dispute. 
Stay application stands disposed of 
accordingly.
 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
22.05.2025
Avneet/

Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel for respondent 
nos.1 & 2.
3. Mr. Devendra Pant, learned Standing Counsel for 
the State/respondent no.3.
4. Today, the matter is listed on amendment 
application (IA No.2/2025) whereby the petitioner wants 
to implead the ‘Union of India’ as well as the ‘General 
Officer Commanding in Chief’ as party-respondents in 
the matter.
5. Amendment application is formal in nature and the 
order passed by the proposed respondents is under 
challenge, therefore, the same is not opposed by learned 
counsel for the respondents.
6. Accordingly, the amendment application is allowed.
7. Let necessary amendment be incorporated by 
supplying amended memo of parties within three days.
8. List on 11.05.2026.
9. Interim order dated 22.05.2025 to continue till 
then.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
